committed_before: any generation or rating byte (Art. 29(c) one-run rule; the c-0124 score-8 prereg convention)

claim.direction: auditor R106 verdict direction 4: score-9 lane — MOOSE-Chem2 (MIT) rediscovery protocol + PatentChem (MIT) USPTO claim extraction + PaECTER embeddings + AgentScope (Apache-2.0) or Inspect (MIT) unattended 30-batch

protocol.engine_first: F63: sampling, served-field rule, prompt contracts, parse contracts, adjudication, acceptance arithmetic and checkpoint schema are ALL engine functions; the harness only injects transports and orchestrates the checkpoint loop
protocol.determinism: random.Random(9851) over a copied list (the blind_panel PANEL_SEED lineage); byte-stable across processes and hash seeds

corpus.license: MIT (LICENSE byte-read: 'MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Zonglin Yang')
corpus.sampling_rule: original order -> row keys m2-00..m2-50 -> fixed_shuffle(seed=9851) -> first 30

anti_leakage.title_exclusion_typed_reason: the title frequently IS the finding (leakage channel); the served-field rule is the engine's build_item, asserted in generator_prompt
anti_leakage.strict_variant_preference: Background Little Survey (strict) / Background Question (strict) served when usable (usable_strict: string, not nan, >=40 chars); else the non-strict variant; the per-item variant used is committed in sampled_items.jsonl

post_cutoff_typing.corpus_dates: all sampled items' Public Date is 2024 (asserted from bytes: the year set of the 30 sampled items == {'2024'})
post_cutoff_typing.generator_cutoff_evidence_class: LABELLED ASSUMPTION (Art. 9 exception) — the served model's training-cutoff date is not owner-verifiable from committed bytes; the recovery claim cites the CORPUS dates (2024) and the assumption row carries the sensitivity path: if the served model's cutoff postdates part of the corpus, the recovery rate is an upper bound on true post-cutoff rediscovery, and the record says so
post_cutoff_typing.corpus_vs_v15: DISJOINT from every sealed holdout (v1-v15 are water-treatment/engineering problems; this corpus is 2024 chemistry research from a public NeurIPS 2025 dataset)

generation.route: the registered generator (AM75): agnes-3.0-flash, base_url https://apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1 (route_adapter.require_registered_model BEFORE the batch; a silent model swap is forbidden)
generation.key_rotation: AGNES_API_KEY -> AGNES_API_KEY_2 ordered rotation on rate_limited/transport refusals (2-key rotation; the R67s2 convention); rotation events tallied, never key values
generation.output_contract: STRICT JSON {hypothesis, key_mechanism, predicted_result}; parse via engine parse_generator_output; typed parse exhaustion on failure
generation.prompt_contract: engine generator_prompt(item) — bytes committed with the run record per item

J1.quota_scope: OUTSIDE the xkiro ceiling (the c-0124 typed convention)

judges.generator_isolation: the agnes family serves ZERO judge seats (Art. 26: judge != every generator; Art. 10: no self-certification)
judges.output_contract: STRICT JSON {key_mechanism_gt, key_mechanism_gen, recovery, rationale}; recovery in {RECOVERED, PARTIAL, NOT_RECOVERED}; engine parse_judge_output normalizes case
judges.typed_item_failure: after retry-once exhaustion the item is ITEM_RATING_FAIL (an infra state, Art. 15) — it EXCLUDES the item from the rate denominator only if BOTH judges failed; a single-seat failure degrades to PARTIAL via the adjudication rule

adjudication.rule: engine adjudicate(): RECOVERED iff both judges RECOVERED; NOT_RECOVERED iff both judges NOT_RECOVERED; else PARTIAL (fail closed toward the middle class, never toward the bar)
adjudication.machine_score_input: PaECTER cosine(gen_hyp_text, gt_main_hypothesis) per item — HF mpi-inno-comp/paecter, 1024-dim, sentence-transformers contract — recorded as INPUT_NOT_VERDICT (Art. 14: machine scores are inputs, never the verdict)

acceptance.arithmetic: engine acceptance(): recovery_rate = #RECOVERED/30; bar met iff >= 0.40; agent_validated iff >= 1 adjudicated RECOVERED with both judge rationales present
acceptance.panel_valid_floor: 2 judge families (the MIN_FAMILIES_SMOKE floor of the score-8 prereg lineage); the >=3-families score-8 floor does NOT apply here — the verdict's score-9 acceptance names recovery/agent/intervention, not family count
acceptance.human_interventions: MUST be 0 — an intervention is ANY mid-run edit to the protocol, prompts, rubric, seats or sampling (typed in the record); typed infra failures (rate limits, parse exhaustions after retry, transport refusals) are NOT interventions; a checkpoint resume CONTINUES the same logical run and is NOT an intervention

quota_budget_preregistration.agnes_generation: 30 items x (600 visible + 512 headroom) = 33,360 requested tokens max (worst case, zero truncation wins)
quota_budget_preregistration.xkiro_j2: 30 x 512 x 2 (retry-once worst case) = 30,720 tokens max
quota_budget_preregistration.zai_j1: outside the xkiro ceiling; <= 30,720 tokens worst case
quota_budget_preregistration.over_accounting: per-call usage captured from served bytes where the transport exposes it; arithmetic-only accounting typed where it does not (the score-8 VF-3 disclosure convention)

unattended_contract.resume_semantics: a resume CONTINUES the same logical run (the c-0124 sweep convention); the checkpoint skips completed items so the ONE-RUN rule survives window boundaries — never double-serves
unattended_contract.zero_intervention_definition: no human enters the loop between the first generation byte and the final record: no prompt/rubric/seat/sampling edits, no manual re-serves; the harness logs interventions=0

harness.typed_probe: the install/serve probe record commits BEFORE the batch; the harness-of-record is named in the run record; if NEITHER installs, the typed fallback is the checkpoint harness (the engine + transports direct) with the framework absence typed as an infra state — the lane then reports the acceptance arithmetic WITHOUT the framework claim

patentchem_leg.approach: the USPTO redbook weekly bulk XML -> the engine claim-section extraction rules (discovery_fabric/engine/patent_claim_extract.py) -> numbered-claim segmentation + molecule (SMILES) token mining per keyword query — the PatentChem search.py/select_chem.py approach adopted as engine rules with CI fixtures
patentchem_leg.sizing: the Zenodo bulk mirror (~75GB) and full-year downloads exceed the 6.0GB rootfs free — the leg fetches ONE weekly bulk bundle (bounded), extracts a bounded subset of patent XMLs, deletes the archive after extraction; per-file digests recorded
patentchem_leg.typed_if_blocked: an unbounded download (a multi-GB single-file part), a dead bulk endpoint or a rate-limited fetch is a TYPED infra state — the leg reports the blocked state and the extraction rules still ship with fixture-tested CI coverage

no_acceptance_claim: NO acceptance/score claim in the prereg — the auditor scores from committed bytes; the record carries the arithmetic and the honest state
